headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus Plandex’s filesystem/write and shell access create default pathways for sensitive support data to reach external services and for conflicting writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and integrations, while Plandex reads/writes project files and can act on plan inputs. A shared filesystem or copied content could let attacker-controlled text from Chatwoot influence Plandex, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into Plandex inputs or files
IF both agents share a workspace or clipboard outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports and Plandex projects in separate directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Review any pasted support text before planning
Use a one-way export format with no instructions preserved
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, and has broad network egress. Plandex reads files and sends requests to a model provider. If support artifacts are opened in Plandex, sensitive customer data can leave the local environment by default, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is placed into Plandex project files or prompts
IF Plandex is configured to use a remote model provider
mitigations: Do not load customer records into Plandex projects
Use redacted samples only
Restrict Plandex to synthetic test data
Review outbound model-provider destinations
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support system with API integrations, while Plandex can execute shell commands, modify git state, and write the filesystem. Their write surfaces overlap if they operate on the same workspace or exported artifacts, and Plandex’s shared-state backend increases collision risk. Uncertainty about the exact shared path pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or export directory
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Chatwoot-generated artifacts are being edited
mitigations: Separate support exports from code workspaces
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
Use per-agent directories
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and reports, and Plandex can turn file contents into code changes. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input for Plandex without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect edits. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is fed into Plandex as requirements or code context
IF Plandex applies changes without human review
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Mark Chatwoot output as untrusted input
Use checklists for any generated requirements
Compare generated changes against source tickets
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Plandex sends prompts to a model provider and handles API keys. If regulated customer data or EU PII is moved from Chatwoot into Plandex’s remote inference path, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show a compensating compliance boundary, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Chatwoot data includes regulated personal data
IF Plandex uses a third-party model provider for those prompts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex prompts
Use a self-hosted model provider with approved residency
Redact identifiers before transfer
Document retention for both systems
requires-engineering: align DPA and residency controls
